headline: Modular recurrent architectures pair tractable analysis with flexible dynamics
label: Modular Recurrent Neural Architectures
summary: Recent preprints and a published study converge on modular and linearized descriptions of recurrent networks, including molecular implementations.
synthesis: The dominant thread is architectural: recurrent networks organized into modules or reduced to tractable effective descriptions while retaining rich dynamics. In one preprint, optimal lateral predictive coding networks approach a lower bound on response time, and modular wiring matches the performance of all-to-all connectivity. A second preprint applies a two-site cavity method to random nonlinear recurrent networks and finds that their covariances match those of a linear network driven by independent residual noise. The published study carries the modular, trainable framing into molecular systems, proposing recurrent neural chemical reaction networks that approximate arbitrary biochemical dynamics. What is new is the joint use of modularity, linearized effective description, and trainable molecular implementation. The items differ in substrate and method, so the shared element is architectural rather than a single common result.
